item.title: Spaces, commas, and other things that go bump in filenames (at the command-line)
item.author: Joel Graber
item.description:
Spaces, commas, and other things that go bump in filenames (at the command-line)

Today’s tip for those of you who are trying to learn to work from the command-line (or who might ever send a file to me).

When it comes to filenames, spaces, commas, and pretty much anything that isn’t either a letter (a-z, A-Z), number (0-9), dash (-), underscore (_), or period (.) are EVIL and SHOULD BE AVOIDED.
item.source: Comparative Genomics and Data Science Core

item.title: Resources for learning to operate a computer from the command-line
item.author: Joel Graber
item.description:
Resources for learning to operate a computer from the command-line

Much of the work that we do in computational biology operates from what we call “the command-line” interface. The command-line allows us to carry out nearly all of the operations that you can with a graphical user interface (GUI), with its “point-and-click” interface. In many cases, (e.g., in launching large-scale computational processes, such as needed for genomic data analysis), it is much more efficient to do so from the command-line, especially if you are going to be using cloud-based or other remote computing resources.
item.source: Comparative Genomics and Data Science Core
